description: Linux namespaces + cgroups decomposed. The 8 namespace types. cgroup v1 vs v2 differences. unshare, clone(CLONE_NEW*), setns. The 'isolated view' (namespaces) + 'resource budget' (cgroups) combination that constitutes a container. How runc / containerd build containers from these primitives.

sub_mechanisms.name: PID_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Isolates process ID space. PID 1 inside namespace is the namespace's init; outside it's a normal PID.
sub_mechanisms.why: Container's processes can't see (or signal) host processes. Container's PID 1 reaps orphans within the namespace. Standard containers have their own PID 1.

sub_mechanisms.name: mount_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Isolates the mount table. Each namespace has its own /proc, /sys, root filesystem etc.
sub_mechanisms.why: Container has its own filesystem layout. mount inside container doesn't affect host (with private propagation). chroot's modern descendant.

sub_mechanisms.name: network_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Isolates network stack: interfaces, routing tables, firewall rules, /proc/net.
sub_mechanisms.why: Container has its own loopback + virtual interfaces. veth pairs bridge container to host. Container's network configuration is independent. The mechanism enabling Docker, Kubernetes networking.

sub_mechanisms.name: user_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Maps UIDs inside namespace to different UIDs outside. Lets unprivileged user 'be root' inside their own namespace.
sub_mechanisms.why: Rootless containers: container's UID 0 is mapped to host's UID 1000. Container can't actually exercise root privileges on the host. Foundation of unprivileged Docker / Podman.

sub_mechanisms.name: UTS_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Isolates hostname + domain name. uname() returns the namespace's values.
sub_mechanisms.why: Each container can have its own hostname. Trivial isolation but useful for service discovery + logging.

sub_mechanisms.name: IPC_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Isolates System V IPC + POSIX message queues. Resources created in one namespace not visible in another.
sub_mechanisms.why: Legacy IPC isolation. Containers shouldn't see host's shared memory segments etc. Mostly important for older apps using SysV IPC.

sub_mechanisms.name: cgroup_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Isolates cgroup hierarchy view. Container sees its own cgroup as root.
sub_mechanisms.why: Containers manipulating cgroups shouldn't see host's. Enables cgroup-aware tooling inside containers. Added in kernel 4.6.

sub_mechanisms.name: time_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: Isolates clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC + CLOCK_BOOTTIME). Container can have its own monotonic clock offset.
sub_mechanisms.why: Live migration / snapshot restore: container resumed at a different real time can preserve internal time monotonicity. Added in kernel 5.6.

sub_mechanisms.name: cgroup_v1_hierarchy
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each resource controller (cpu, memory, io, etc.) has its own hierarchy. Processes can be in different cgroups in different hierarchies.
sub_mechanisms.why: Legacy design from early cgroup development. Flexibility at cost of complexity + potential inconsistency. Most distros migrating to v2.

sub_mechanisms.name: cgroup_v2_unified
sub_mechanisms.definition: Single hierarchy: process is in one cgroup, period. All controllers (cpu, memory, io) attach to the same hierarchy.
sub_mechanisms.why: Simpler model. Required for some modern features (PSI pressure stalls, io.cost weight-based fair scheduling). Default on most distros since systemd v246+.

sub_mechanisms.name: cgroup_cpu_controller
sub_mechanisms.definition: Limits + accounts CPU time. cpu.weight (proportional sharing) or cpu.max (hard quota: 50000 100000 = 50ms per 100ms).
sub_mechanisms.why: Container CPU limits. Hard caps for predictable behaviour; weights for fair sharing. CFS integrates with this for proportional scheduling.

sub_mechanisms.name: cgroup_memory_controller
sub_mechanisms.definition: Limits + accounts RAM. memory.max (hard limit), memory.high (soft, reclaim pressure), memory.low (protected).
sub_mechanisms.why: Container memory budgets. memory.max breach triggers OOM-kill within the cgroup. memory.high enables more graceful degradation under pressure.

sub_mechanisms.name: clone_CLONE_NEW_flags
sub_mechanisms.definition: clone() / unshare() with CLONE_NEWPID, CLONE_NEWNET, etc. flags create or detach the calling process into new namespaces.
sub_mechanisms.why: The syscall interface to namespace creation. Container runtimes (runc) call clone with appropriate flags to create the container's namespaces atomically with the child process.

sub_mechanisms.name: setns_join_namespace
sub_mechanisms.definition: setns(fd, type) syscall: join an existing namespace (referenced by fd from /proc/PID/ns/*).
sub_mechanisms.why: Tools entering existing namespaces (nsenter, docker exec). The fd-based interface lets you reference a namespace even if no process is in it.

derivation_rules.name: containers_are_namespaces_plus_cgroups
if: a process has its own PID/mount/net namespaces AND is in a resource-limited cgroup
derivation_rules.why: Container ≡ isolated view + resource budget. No magic 'container' kernel object — it's the combination of these primitives. runc / podman / docker assemble these into the container abstraction.

derivation_rules.name: user_namespace_enables_rootless_containers
if: root in a container is mapped to a normal UID on host
then: container can't exercise root privileges on host
derivation_rules.why: Container's UID 0 is host's UID 100000 (e.g.). Container believes it's root; kernel checks capabilities against host UID. Foundation of rootless Docker, Podman, lightweight container security.

derivation_rules.name: cgroup_v2_single_hierarchy_simpler
if: controllers attach to a unified hierarchy
then: resource limits are consistent across resources
derivation_rules.why: v1 process could be in different cgroups per controller — inconsistent semantics. v2: one cgroup, all controllers see same membership. Required for modern features (PSI, weighted IO).

derivation_rules.name: container_overhead_proportional_to_namespaces_used
if: a container uses only some namespaces (e.g., PID + mount but shares network)
then: overhead is only for the used namespaces
derivation_rules.why: Containers compose primitives. Shared network = sees host's network. Use the minimum namespaces needed for isolation. Kubernetes pods share network namespace among containers — they're 'partial containers' with shared net.

derivation_rules.name: cgroup_limits_strictly_enforced
then: processes in the cgroup cannot allocate beyond N total
derivation_rules.why: Kernel checks at allocation time. Exceeding triggers OOM-killer within the cgroup. The strict enforcement is what makes containers safe — host can run many containers without one consuming all resources.
